plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant evergreen shrub with silvery-green narrow leaves and dense spikes of small tubular flowers. It is widely grown in gardens, and commercially for essential oils, perfumes and culinary use. Bees and butterflies are strongly attracted to its nectar-rich blooms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-June to August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, Tasmania and the United States
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Latin 'lavare' meaning 'to wash', as the Romans used lavender to scent their baths.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a rough, hairy stem and a huge flower head made of many tiny florets surrounded by yellow ray petals. The flower heads track the sun when young. It is grown for seeds, oil and ornament, and is a favorite of pollinators and birds.
plants.bloomingSeason: July to September in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to North America; widely cultivated in Ukraine, Russia, Argentina, Europe and the United States
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds follow the sun across the sky (heliotropism), but mature flowers typically face east permanently, which warms them early and attracts more pollinators.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large round leaves that repel water and showy, fragrant flowers held above the water's surface on tall stalks. It grows in shallow ponds, lakes and wetlands, and is revered in many Asian cultures as a symbol of purity.
plants.bloomingSeason: June to September in temperate Asia
plants.location: Native to Asia and Australia; found in India, China, Japan, Vietnam and the Volga Delta in Russia
plants.funFact: Lotus seeds can remain viable for centuries; seeds around 1,300 years old recovered from a dry lakebed in China were successfully germinated.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A shrub with the largest flower head of any protea, made up of a central cone of tiny flowers surrounded by showy, pointed bracts. It thrives in the nutrient-poor, acidic soils of the fynbos, and is pollinated by beetles and birds. It is the national flower of South Africa.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to spring, with peak flowering in the Southern Hemisphere winter, including July and August
plants.location: Native to the fynbos of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: Protea is named after the Greek god Proteus, who could change his shape, reflecting the great diversity of forms in the genus.
